obligation.exact_statement: For every K>=2, fixed beta>0 and fixed D1 theta, extend the admitted causal Route A family with reference P_(N,s)=(A_N(s,.)+lambda_N v0)/(u_s+lambda_N), lambda_N=1/(N-2), into an explicit general-D1 finite-history TV upper theorem with a theta-independent parameter/accuracy schedule. Derive a simultaneous concentration event for all K^3 legal empirical transition frequencies, keeping structural zeros and explicit dependence on eta_theta=min p_theta, pi_s, N and failure probability. On this single path event, combine sampling, smoothing, actual finite frontend/correction errors, and declared located perturbations without treating q,r,u sampling fluctuations independently or asserting a universal u^{-2} gain. Declare the full visible representation and all copies. Include actual terminal-query conditional risk and correctly stationary-weighted actual average risk, without assuming query/history independence. Give explicit deterministic bounds mapping bounded errors in the two charged local copied symbol blocks, Q/K scores, post-aggregation q/r/mu and query-context residual into the implemented frequency selector and probability output; keep discrete masks/length/type fixed unless explicitly analyzed. Account for finite rational input caps at every perturbed location and preserve an exact simplex output. Prove the required uniform numerical-softmax estimate on the declared perturbed score interval, either within the admitted backend or via an explicitly charged legal extension preserving nominal fixed beta and the original unperturbed consistency guarantee. State a concrete finite resource envelope (L,W,H,D_qk,B_param,B_arith,score_range) for the chosen mechanism and the admitted strong direct-correction comparison, including any changed exponent approximation and all retained residuals. Report exactly which perturbation sites are covered, distinguish operator-only or additional layer-error claims from proved finite-code guarantees, and state meaningful nonempty robustness conditions. This is a finite-history/located-error upper theorem, not an optimal sample-rate or precision lower bound, unrestricted architecture claim, log-loss theorem, or C1-C4/root closure.
